experience.reason: The shift into visceral body horror ("ribs are my architecture") feels tonally jarring and gratuitous compared to the preceding psychological intimacy, breaking the thematic consistency of "wanting" with shock value.

The shift to visceral, body-horror imagery ("ribs are my architecture") feels tonally disjointed from the preceding metaphysical melancholy, breaking the established thematic consistency. It sacrifices the psychological subtlety of the "Voyd" for shock value that lacks narrative grounding.

The sudden shift to visceral body horror and the Voyd’s predatory possession breaks the established psychological intimacy, feeling like a tonal mismatch rather than a logical escalation of the theme of "wanting."

The sudden, jarring shift to visceral, biological imagery ("four small lights press against my ribs") breaks the established psychological and metaphysical tone, confusing the reader rather than deepening the thematic exploration of regret.
